subject: Reserved capacity: tenor safeguard proposal and GPU-cost pass-through escalation
messages:
From: Sam Park <sam.park@cortexai.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Meyers <jordan.meyers@cortexai-legal.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity conversation follow-up

Connor — thanks for the call earlier. CortexAI is supportive of moving to a reserved block but procurement has two asks before they can sign: (1) a clearer mechanism for GPU-cost pass-through if market spot/kubernetes pricing increases more than 15% year-over-year, and (2) a mid-term adjustment window (at 12 months) where they can request a +/- 20% rebalancing of SKUs if workload mix shifts. They asked if Redwood can offer a short form clause that protects them from extreme price spikes while giving you runway for planning.

They also want to see the price-sensitivity model you ran during the demo (the one comparing T4 to A100 mixes). Can you send that and a draft term sheet? Sam

[No attachments in this initial email]

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Sam Park <sam.park@cortexai.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Nov 2025 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity conversation follow-up

Sam — thanks for outlining their asks, this is exactly the level of detail we needed.

Quick responses:
- We can provide the sensitivity workbook and a drafted term clause that includes a capped pass-through trigger. I'm attaching a proposed draft and the model we used. The draft includes a 20% market-shock trigger (i.e., if average supplier index moves >20% vs baseline, a negotiated surcharge option is available) and an optional credit if prices move favorably.
- For the mid-term rebalance window, we usually allow a single reallocation request with the reserved block kept constant; I'd like to propose an explicit +/-20% SKU rebalance at month 12 with a reconciliation of unit economics (no retroactive credit unless both parties agree).

I'll need internal signoff on the trigger level and whether we allow automatic pass-through vs. an exec-escalation path. Looping Neha and Karthik for finance/legal lens.

Attachments: [reserved_commit_term_draft.pdf (PDF), gpu-price-sensitivity-model.xlsx (Excel)]

—Connor
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Nov 2025 08:33:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Reserved capacity conversation follow-up

Connor — reviewed the draft and the sensitivity workbook. Notes below (finance perspective):

1) Trigger threshold — 20% is aggressive (protects Redwood too much). Recommend 15% threshold for automatic review, with a 20% threshold qualifying for an accelerated exec review that can result in a temporary surcharge or credit. This gives both sides a graded response.

2) Adjustment mechanics — if we allow a reallocation at month 12 (+/-20%), we must include a one-time reconciliation settlement (positive or negative) based on realized utilization vs. baseline forecast. Suggest reconciliation be capped at 3 months of invoice exposure to limit P&L volatility.

3) Discount ask — CortexAI is requesting a 18% committed discount on list for a 24-month tenor. Finance is willing to entertain 12–15% for a 24-month, 18% requires an exec exception (VP finance). If you want 18%, I need the deal economics (ARR, expected consumption ramp) to build the approval memo.

I attached a simplified sensitivity slice for quick exec review.

-Neha
Head of Revenue Finance
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: gpu-price-sensitivity-model.xlsx (trimmed) ]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Nov 2025 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Reserved capacity conversation follow-up

Legal/ops points from my side:

- Pass-through language: recommend an "escalator" clause that specifies a joint-review process. Automatic surcharge clauses risk customer pushback and create renewal friction. Proposed flow: (a) trigger detected -> (b) internal notice + run reconciliation model -> (c) 14-day exec review window to propose adjustment (surcharge/credit/term amendment) -> (d) if parties can't agree, default to a 3-month price-hold while both parties arbitrate with a pre-agreed mediator.

- Rebalancing: require a 30-day notice window for any SKU reallocation, and a cap on frequency (one-time at month 12). Also call out compatibility of fallback model variants (we can guarantee latency tiers for equivalent SKU mixes).

- Approvals: anything >16% discount needs VP/Head Sales approval; >17% requires CRO sign-off. If you're pushing for 18% (per Cortex ask), I will prepare redlines that preserve the escalator and require a firm P&L approval path.

-Karthik
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Sam Park <sam.park@cortexai.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 7 Nov 2025 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Reserved capacity conversation follow-up

Sam — sharing a revised short-form clause and a clear set of options so Cortex can choose the comfort level they want. Options included in the attached PDF:
- Option A (Balanced): 15% sensitivity threshold, joint review, reconciliation capped at 3 months invoice, one-time 12-month SKU rebalance allowed, 14-day exec review window. Pricing: 14% committed discount for 24 months.
- Option B (Customer-protective): 10% threshold, no automatic surcharge (credit-only remediation), limited SKU rebalance, Pricing: 12% committed discount.
- Option C (Provider-protective): 20% threshold with automatic surcharge up to a negotiated cap, Pricing: 16% committed discount.

Cortex can pick their preferred option and we will route approvals internally. If they want Option A but still insist on 18% discount, note that will require VP finance + CRO approval and we will need a 36-month commitment or larger committed consumption to justify.

Please confirm which option they prefer and if they want finance execs looped in directly.

Attachments: [reserved_commit_term_draft.pdf] 

—Connor
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Sam Park <sam.park@cortexai.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 9 Nov 2025 16:47:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Reserved capacity conversation follow-up

Connor / team — CortexAI prefers Option A (15% threshold, joint review, 3-month reconciliation cap) but asks for an explicit mechanism to convert reconciliation outcomes into credits if pricing moves favorably (they won't accept unilateral surcharges without the possibility of credit). They are comfortable with the one-time 12-month SKU rebalance.

On the discount: they will take 14% for 24 months if we commit to an annual review with a 60-day mutual notice period around expected ramp changes. They asked if you can put together an approval path for the 16% scenario if they move to a 36-month contract or increase committed GPU-hours by 35% Year 1.

Jordan (legal) from their side is available to do a redline pass next week.

Thanks,
Sam
Head of Infrastructure, CortexAI
